// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=Moq&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using System.Runtime.CompilerServices;

// Everything here runs once, when the test assembly loads, before any test.
public static class ModuleInitializer
{
    [ModuleInitializer]
    public static void Initialize()
    {
        // Initializes every Verify.* plugin the project references and has not initialized above.
        // Explicit calls come first so their parameters apply: a plugin can only be initialized once.
        VerifierSettings.InitializePlugins();
    }
}

==== src/VerifySample.Tests/Extensions/MoqTests.cs

// Generated by the Verify wizard: https://verifytests.github.io/Wizard/new?step=output&os=Windows&ide=Rider&cli=Cli&tf=XunitV3&ci=GitHubActions&ext=Moq&sponsor=Exempt&exempt=OpenSource&until=2027-09
// Delete whatever is not needed.
using Moq;

// Verify.Moq: Snapshots a Moq mock: the calls it received, their named arguments and what each one returned.
// https://github.com/VerifyTests/Verify.Moq
// Note: Verify the Mock<T>, not mock.Object: the converter is registered for the mock.
// Note: The package has no net10.0 target framework, so a newer project resolves the net9.0
// assets.
public class MoqTests
{
    // The mock itself is verified, not a call list. The snapshot names each argument and
    // includes the value returned, which is what Moq records and the others do not.
    [Fact]
    public Task RecordedInvocations()
    {
        var mock = new Mock<ITarget>();

        mock.Setup(_ => _.Method(It.IsAny<int>(), It.IsAny<int>()))
            .Returns("response");

        var target = mock.Object;
        target.Method(1, 2);
        return Verify(mock);
    }

    // Arguments are recorded under their parameter names, so one that changes per run is
    // dropped by name with ScrubMember from Verify core.
    [Fact]
    public Task ScrubArguments()
    {
        var mock = new Mock<ITarget>();

        mock.Setup(_ => _.Method(It.IsAny<int>(), It.IsAny<int>()))
            .Returns("response");

        var target = mock.Object;
        target.Method(1, 2);
        return Verify(mock)
            .ScrubMember("a");
    }
}
